tonight.headline: Josh Allen banked 40.8 last night and Panda Attack have not played a single player yet.
body: Allen went for 40.8 against Detroit, 17.9 above his 22.9 projection, and it is the only score on the board in this matchup. Panda Attack moved Dalton Kincaid out of their tight end slot before kickoff and started Harold Fannin Jr., so they took nothing out of Thursday night. ESPN's live model still only gives you 59%, which is the honest number: a 40-point lead over an unplayed roster is one good Sunday from being gone.

There is nothing to do about this matchup today. Your lineup is the one this brief would write, and the only card below is a bench move that has nothing to do with the score. Come back to the roster on Sunday morning once Friday's designations exist.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Panda Attack start three running backs — Chase Brown, Saquon Barkley and Javonte Williams in the RB/WR flex — for 50.0 projected against your 28.6 from Achane and Warren. Saquon is the specific problem: Tennessee were D/ST28 in Week 1 and allowed the Jets 152 rushing yards, the seventh-most of any team. If he goes for 25 the gap you banked last night is half gone before their receivers play.

case.label: Where it actually turns
case.body: Davante Adams and Harrison Mevis play Monday night at the Rams, and so does your Isaiah Likely. Roughly 31 of their projected points and 11 of yours resolve after Sunday finishes. If this is close on Sunday evening, Likely against a 48.5-point total is your side of that trade and it is a good side to have.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Panda Attack set a different lineup before Sunday — Jalen Hurts is sitting on their bench at 20.1 behind Dak Prescott at 20.3, and if they swap for any reason the projection gap moves against you by a point with no warning. Rival lineup changes are visible only after the fact in the activity log.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Atlanta kick off Sun 11:00 Mexico City — after that Pitts cannot be dropped
doFirst.title: Drop Kyle Pitts, add Mack Hollins
doFirst.subtitle: Third run carrying this card. Atlanta's quarterback answer moved against Pitts overnight, not for him.

case.label: The drop, which is the whole card
case.body: Chem's flex is slot 3, RB/WR only. Isaiah Likely holds the one tight end slot on a thesis that got stronger this week — 8 catches on 8 targets, 78 yards and two touchdowns in his Giants debut, with Malik Nabers still conditioning. Pitts cannot enter your lineup in any week Likely is available, so his 10.4 projection is unreachable and his effective projection is zero. STRATEGY.md section 9 says it in a line: a second startable tight end has value in IPADE and none here.

case.label: What changed since yesterday
case.body: Yesterday's brief told you Michael Penix Jr. was Atlanta's questionable starter. That was wrong and I am correcting it: the Falcons depth chart released 15 September has Penix fourth string, still recovering from ACL surgery, and Tua Tagovailoa listed first with Cooper Rush behind him. Then on 16 September Kevin Stefanski said Tua would not practise that day with an oblique and that he was 'not ruling anyone out'. SI's weekly starter list, updated for Week 2, has Cooper Rush. I take Rush. That is the exact configuration that produced a 0.0 from Pitts the week this system learned to check who is throwing.

case.label: The add, and who it is contested with
case.body: A.J. Brown is on injured reserve for New England for six games. Yahoo's positional column this week says Mack Hollins 'slid into Brown's role the moment Brown limped to the medical tent', took 18 of the first 32 snaps and went 4 for 51, and drew a fourth-down target late in a one-score game. Six games is a role with a season-shaped clock on it, not a one-week streamer.

case.label: Where I take a side against my own source
case.body: The same Yahoo writer predicts Hollins leads the room and then votes for DeMario Douglas, who had a team-high 7 targets for 5 catches and 20 yards. I take Hollins on role over Douglas on volume: 20 yards on 7 targets is a slot floor, not a ceiling, and Hollins is the one who inherited the alignment. Romeo Doubs is the name the market likes — 61% rostered nationally and free here — and he is the fade: 40 snaps, zero catches, drops and an interception on a four-year, $68m contract. He is in Do-not-chase below.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Isaiah Likely appears on the Giants' Friday or Saturday injury report — New York play Monday, so those reports land after this brief — which would make Pitts the only tight end on the roster and this card wrong the same hour. Or Guillo-tinas rule George Kittle out, which turns Pitts from dead weight into the only trade chip on this roster; Kittle was limited Wednesday with the Achilles, which is trending the other way. Or New England's Friday report names Douglas or Doubs rather than Hollins as the man absorbing Brown's work.

whatWentWrong.title: I told you yesterday that Michael Penix Jr. was Atlanta's questionable quarterback. He is fourth string.
whatWentWrong.lead: Penix is recovering from ACL surgery and was inactive in Week 1. The real Atlanta question is Tua Tagovailoa's oblique against Cooper Rush, and Rush is the likelier answer.

case.label: What the error was
case.body: Yesterday's Pitts row read 'Michael Penix Jr. questionable'. The Falcons' 15 September depth chart has Tua first, Rush second, Jack Strand third and Penix fourth. Penix's questionable tag is real but it is a fourth-string tag, and treating it as the starter's tag made Atlanta look like a team one designation away from being fine.

case.label: Why it matters to the card above
case.body: It cuts in the direction of the card, not against it. Cooper Rush threw for 143 yards with an interception and a pick-six in Week 1. A Pitts whose quarterback is Rush is worth less than a Pitts whose quarterback is Penix, so the drop is easier today than it was yesterday. The error was in the evidence, not the conclusion, and it is still an error.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Tua practising Thursday or Friday and being named the starter. Then Atlanta's passing game is a different proposition and Pitts's trade value — not his lineup value, which is zero here regardless — comes back.

whatWentWrong.title: The Pitts card is now forty-four hours old and he is still on your bench
whatWentWrong.lead: Written Wednesday as DEPTH, raised to SOLID Thursday, carried again today. Atlanta kick off Sunday at 11:00 Mexico City and a player whose game has started cannot be dropped.

case.label: What it has cost
case.body: Nothing yet, because Pitts has not played since the card was written. That is luck. The cost arrives at 11:00 Sunday, when the seat locks for the week and cannot be used for anyone — including for Mark Andrews, if the Giants put Likely on their Saturday report.

case.label: Why it keeps not happening
case.body: The card asks you to drop a 93.5%-rostered tight end for a 6.5%-rostered receiver. It reads wrong at a glance and it is right on the structure. That is a presentation problem in my card rather than an error in it, which is why this is the second time it appears in this section.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: You deciding not to make it. If Pitts is still here Sunday at 11:00 I close the thesis CHURN on Tuesday and stop rewriting it, and the bench seat gets planned around him instead.

worthALook.name: Mark Andrews
worthALook.lead: The biggest ownership anomaly on either wire, free here, and the trigger that would make him a card has not fired.

case.label: The trigger, checked this run
case.body: The condition on the record was: Isaiah Likely appears on a Giants injury report. He does not. The Giants' Thursday report, 17 September, lists Adebo as the only non-participant and six limited players, none of them Likely and none of them Nabers. New York play Monday, so their Friday and Saturday reports land after this brief.

case.label: What research took off him
case.body: Andrews went 4 for 49 in Baltimore's opener, functioning as the second option behind Zay Flowers, and dropped an easy ball on second-and-goal. He is not the player Likely was in Week 1 and the 169.4 season projection against Likely's 156.2 is the sort of gap STRATEGY says not to transact on.

case.label: Why he still is not a card
case.body: Chem's flex is RB/WR. Andrews sits behind Likely in the one tight end slot, so adding him recreates exactly the dead seat the Pitts card is clearing. He is the best available player on this wire and he does not fit this roster; both are true at once.

case.label: When to act
case.body: The hour Likely appears on a Giants report — Saturday is the realistic day — or if Likely draws under four targets at the Rams on Monday. Either makes Andrews the starter rather than the second tight end, and he is a free agent so it costs nothing but the seat.

worthALook.name: Khalil Shakir
worthALook.lead: 69% rostered nationally and sitting on waivers here, clearing Wednesday — and by then his value is a Week 3 question, not a Week 2 one.

case.label: Why he is on this list
case.body: This is the why=OWNED band, the strongest single wire signal in a 10-team league: widely rostered elsewhere, available here. FantasyPros named him a Week 2 sleeper on the reasoning that Buffalo–Detroit would be a high-scoring Thursday game, and it was — Josh Allen went for 40.8 in it.

case.label: The number that complicates it
case.body: He clears at 01:00 Mexico City on Wednesday 23 September, which is after his Week 2 game has already been played. Nothing about his Week 2 line is claimable. You would be claiming a Week 3 asset off a Week 2 sleeper note, and the note is spent.

case.label: What it costs
case.body: Nothing lasting. Chem waiver priority resets weekly, so a claim here is free even from 10th. That is the whole reason he is worth listing rather than dismissing.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Tuesday, after his Week 2 line exists. If he clears six targets against Detroit, claim him on Wednesday with the drop being whoever of Monangai or Brian Thomas Jr. has the worse Sunday. If he does not, he is a name on a list.

worthALook.name: Woody Marks
worthALook.lead: Carried unchanged from yesterday, and unchanged is the finding: no dated Week 2 Houston usage report was retrievable again.

case.label: The standing case
case.body: 55% rostered nationally and free here, with reporting that has him passing Nick Chubb during Joe Mixon's absence. A CBS note says he is 'unlikely to see his workload increase'. Those two reads have not been reconciled by anything published this week.

case.label: The seat problem
case.body: There is none. Coker's seat is frozen until 22 September, the tight end seat is the Pitts card, and the other three bench places hold players carrying Friday designations. Claiming him means dropping a questionable player before his designation exists, which is the mistake this log calls the Monangai mistake.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Houston naming him the lead back on a Friday or Saturday report, or Jaylen Warren or De'Von Achane appearing on an injury report — which turns a speculative claim into one for a real hole. By 22 September he is a free agent here anyway and the claim is free.

doNotChase.name: Romeo Doubs
doNotChase.lead: He was on this brief's watch list yesterday as SOLID. Today's reporting says fade him, and I am saying so rather than quietly dropping the row.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Forty snaps and zero catches in Week 1. Not zero targets — zero catches, with drops and an interception thrown his way, on a four-year, $68 million contract. Mack Hollins played 18 of the first 32 snaps and caught four for 51 in the same game.

case.label: Why the ownership is a trap here
case.body: 61% rostered nationally and free in Chem reads like the ownership anomaly STRATEGY section 4 calls the strongest wire signal. It is not one. That band works when a manager blundered; here the national number is priced off the contract and the depth-chart assumption, and the Week 1 snap data says the role went to someone else.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: New England's Friday or Saturday report or beat coverage naming Doubs rather than Hollins or DeMario Douglas as the man absorbing A.J. Brown's six-game absence. That flips the incoming player on the card above without changing the outgoing one.

doNotChase.name: 49ers D/ST
doNotChase.lead: Biggest single-day ownership move on the Chem board again, and the weekly comparison still returns hold.

case.label: The comparison, which is the point of this row
case.body: Pro Football Network's Week 2 board: San Francisco D/ST6, Baltimore D/ST9. ESPN project San Francisco 7.8 and Baltimore 7.6 in this league's scoring. Three places and two tenths of a point. The Chargers, also free here, are D/ST3 — a bigger gap and a genuinely better draw against Las Vegas.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Two tenths, against a seat that changed hands on 16 September. The churn rule closes this seat until 22 September and STRATEGY forbids proposing a move worth under a point. Baltimore also draw the softest offence on the slate: New Orleans are named a must-sit defence to face and Baltimore scored 41 in Week 1.

case.label: Where the boards disagree
case.body: Yesterday this brief cited FantasyPros with Baltimore 3rd and San Francisco 4th. PFN today has 9th and 6th. Both boards keep Baltimore inside the top ten and neither produces a point of gain, so the disagreement does not change the answer — but it is worth knowing the tile is built on a board rather than on a settled rank.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore finishing outside the top twelve defensive scores in Week 2 while San Francisco or the Chargers finish top five. Then the churn rule cost real points, the seat opens on Tuesday 22 September, and the Chargers are first on the list, not San Francisco.

doNotChase.name: Jordan Addison
doNotChase.lead: Declined for the fourth consecutive run, and the quarterback clause that was supposed to rescue him has now resolved against him twice.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Ownership is falling, now -0.45 on the day and negative on every snapshot this week. A 75%-rostered receiver whose national ownership is dropping is a market walking away, not one that has not noticed.

case.label: The clause, resolved
case.body: The condition was: Kyler Murray clears protocol and Addison draws seven or more targets. Murray is still in protocol, ESPN project him 0.0, and Carson Wentz is the likelier starter. Wentz threw Jefferson 8 of 9 in Week 1. Addison is the third read in an offence whose second read is already on your roster.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jefferson missing time. Nothing short of that makes the second Minnesota receiver a starter on a roster that already holds the first one, and if Jefferson misses time you are buying Addison for a different reason entirely.

settled.title: Hold Isaiah Likely over Kyle Pitts at tight end (14 September)
settled.result: Holding hard. 8 catches on 8 targets, 78 yards and two touchdowns in the Giants debut, with Nabers still conditioning, and ClutchPoints have him a Week 2 start at the Rams. The corollary — Pitts is dead weight in this league — is the card at the top.

settled.title: Tell you Michael Penix Jr. was Atlanta's questionable starter (17 September)
settled.result: Wrong. Penix is fourth string off ACL surgery. Atlanta's Week 2 choice is Tua's oblique against Cooper Rush, and SI's list says Rush. Corrected in What went wrong above.

settled.title: List Romeo Doubs as a SOLID watch-list name (17 September)
settled.result: Wrong, and reversed today. Forty snaps and zero catches in Week 1 with drops and an interception. He is in Do-not-chase below instead.

settled.title: Start Terry McLaurin in the RB/WR flex over Bhayshul Tuten (15 September)
settled.result: Held, and it got closer. Dallas allowed the most fantasy points to receivers in 2025, which is the best draw McLaurin has had; Denver missed 28 tackles, which is the best draw Tuten has had. McLaurin's 12.6 against 10.1 and his 92.1% route share keep him in the slot, but this is now a one-point call, not a comfortable one.

settled.title: Hold Tyler Loop at kicker (16 September)
settled.result: Held, fourth consecutive run. PFN have Loop K4. Best available on this wire is Chase McLaughlin K6, then Trey Smack K13 and Cairo Santos K14. Tyler Bass is K8 and sitting on waivers here, and K8 does not beat K4.

settled.title: Hold the Ravens defence rather than churn to San Francisco (16 September)
settled.result: Held. PFN have Baltimore D/ST9 against New Orleans, who are named a must-sit offence to face. San Francisco at D/ST6 and the Chargers at D/ST3 are both free here and both are Tuesday's question, not today's — the seat is inside the seven-day churn window.

settled.title: Hold Brian Thomas Jr. through the shoulder scare (12 September, reviewed five times)
settled.result: Holding on availability, unproven on production. No Jaguars Friday report was retrievable this run and the one CBS headline that reads like a Week 2 ruling is from a different season. He draws Patrick Surtain II on Sunday.

settled.title: Decline Mark Andrews on structure (17 September)
settled.result: Held, and research strengthened it. Andrews went 4 for 49 as Baltimore's second option behind Zay Flowers and dropped a goal-line ball. The structural objection and the merit objection now point the same way.

settled.title: Claim Jalen Coker, drop Matthew Stafford (14–16 September)
settled.result: Still logged wrong and still not reversed. Coker has been limited three days running with the ankle, Canales expects him to play, and the seat is frozen until 22 September regardless. The cost of the claim was Stafford, who is about to become free in the other league.

cannotSee.label: Friday's designations, which decide three of your five bench players
cannotSee.body: Coker (ankle), Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) and Monangai (knee) all carry questionable tags off Thursday practice. Friday is the report that produces the game designation and it does not exist yet at 07:00 Mexico City. Re-check all three before 11:00 Sunday. This is the single largest thing this brief cannot see.

cannotSee.label: The Giants' Friday and Saturday reports, which are the Mark Andrews trigger
cannotSee.body: New York play Monday night, so their week runs a day later than everyone else's. Likely is absent from Thursday's report. If he appears on Friday's or Saturday's, Mark Andrews goes from watch list to claim the same hour — and if Pitts has already been dropped, the seat for Andrews is the one the Pitts card opened.

cannotSee.label: No Week 2 Chicago participation list, third run running
cannotSee.body: Windy City Gridiron is blocked to automated fetch and no alternative carrying the list was found. Everything published about Monangai's knee that I could retrieve is dated 3–4 September and describes a different injury window; ESPN's own headline about him missing multiple weeks could not be opened. His tile is dashed rather than guessed, and the hold stays UNRESOLVED for the third day.

cannotSee.label: Whether Kyler Murray plays, and that two sources disagree
cannotSee.body: SI's weekly starting-quarterback list, updated for Week 2, prints Kyler Murray for Minnesota. Athlon reported Carson Wentz set to start as the concussion lingers, and ESPN project Murray 0.0 with a questionable tag. I take Wentz because the projection and the injury reporting agree with each other and the list is the slower-moving source. Jefferson's tile survives either way; the margin is thinner if Murray plays cold.

cannotSee.label: Four of the ten grades rest on analyst boards, not on a rank of points allowed
cannotSee.body: Garrett Wilson, Isaiah Likely, the Ravens defence and Tyler Loop are graded off FantasyPros, a game total and PFN's weekly board rather than a published season rank of points allowed to the position. Week 2 is too early for those ranks to be meaningful, which the runbook says outright. Each gradeEvidence line names what it actually rests on.

cannotSee.label: No Chem trade exists, and this is what was tested
cannotSee.body: Yesterday's run scored every one-for-one pairing between your fourteen players and all 126 players on the other nine rosters on both sides' optimal lineups: zero produced a gain for both teams. Two-for-one consolidation produced two, both nonsense - Tuten plus Loop for Cameron Dicker, which trades a flex body for a kicker, and McLaurin plus Pitts for Colston Loveland, which gives up your flex starter for a tight end the RB/WR flex cannot hold. That result is carried forward because no Chem roster has changed since. This run tested the one falsification clause on it directly: Guillo-tinas carry a single tight end, George Kittle, plus Patrick Mahomes stranded behind Lamar Jackson in a one-quarterback league, which is genuine structural surplus. Kittle was limited in practice on Wednesday with an Achilles injury rather than out, so their tight end need is not acute and Pitts is not yet a chip. If Kittle is ruled out on Friday, that changes and the Pitts card above should not be fired.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending waiver claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN only ever returns your own. Mark Andrews at 82% rostered and Khalil Shakir at 69% are the two names most likely to be claimed out from under this brief between now and Wednesday, and there is no way to see it coming.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are still frozen and every trade priced on them is suspect
cannotSee.body: seasonProj produced identical figures across snapshots on three consecutive days for the same players. They do differ correctly between the two leagues — Bo Nix reads 309.6 in Chem and 295.3 in IPADE, which is the scoring-item divergence being applied — so the numbers are computed per league. That is not the same as being updated through the season, and until two snapshots days apart differ, treat every season total here as August's opinion.

cannotSee.label: This brief does not refresh
cannotSee.body: It is as old as the snapshot it was built from: 12:52 UTC on Friday 18 September. Nothing in it updates on its own. The next run is 07:00 Saturday, and Friday's designations will exist by then.
